rules.label: safe
rules.what: Your Windows temporary folder. Apps leave files here and are expected to clean up after themselves.
rules.reclaim: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files, or delete the contents. Files still in use cannot be deleted and are skipped.
rules.notes: Close apps first. Items changed in the last day may belong to something that is running.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: One of many temp folders with the same name prefix, typically left behind by repeated test runs, builds or installers.
rules.reclaim: Delete the folders in this group that are older than a day. The tool that made them recreates what it needs.
rules.notes: Detected by name: at least 5 sibling folders in the temp folder share a prefix.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Working files of Claude Code sessions (scratch folders, task output).
rules.reclaim: Close Claude Code first, then delete it. Folders of sessions that are still running are in use.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: The system-wide temporary folder used by Windows services and installers.
rules.reclaim: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files > Temporary files (needs admin).

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Memory dumps written when apps crashed. Only useful for reporting a crash to a developer.
rules.reclaim: Delete the contents.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Windows Error Reporting: crash and problem reports already sent or queued.
rules.reclaim: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files > Windows error reports.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Windows Update download cache. Updates already installed do not need it.
rules.reclaim: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files > Windows Update Cleanup, or Storage Sense.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Delivery Optimization cache: update pieces kept to share with other PCs.
rules.reclaim: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files > Delivery Optimization Files.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Temporary files from a Windows upgrade or feature update.
rules.reclaim: Disk Cleanup > Clean up system files > Temporary Windows installation files. Do not delete while an upgrade is in progress.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Your previous Windows installation, kept so you can go back after an upgrade.
rules.reclaim: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > Previous Windows installation(s). Removing it means you can no longer roll back.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: The Recycle Bin: files you already deleted.
rules.reclaim: Empty the Recycle Bin (right-click it on the desktop). Check it first if you might want something back.

rules.label: do_not_touch
rules.what: The Windows component store. Much of its apparent size is hard links shared with System32.
rules.reclaim: From an admin prompt: Dism.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup. Never delete files here by hand.

rules.label: do_not_touch
rules.what: Windows Installer cache. Installed programs need these files to update, repair or uninstall.
rules.reclaim: Uninstall programs you no longer use (Settings > Apps > Installed apps); their files here go with them.

rules.label: do_not_touch
rules.what: Windows itself.
rules.reclaim: Use Disk Cleanup (Clean up system files) or Storage Sense. Never delete files here by hand.

rules.label: do_not_touch
rules.what: Windows system file (page file, swap file, hibernation file).
rules.reclaim: Windows manages it. Change its size only in System settings (System > About > Advanced system settings > Performance > Settings > Advanced > Virtual memory); never delete it.
rules.notes: pagefile.sys is the page file; swapfile.sys is the swap file used by Store apps. Both are in use while Windows runs.

rules.label: do_not_touch
rules.what: Windows system file (page file, swap file, hibernation file).
rules.reclaim: Turn hibernation off with powercfg /h off in an admin terminal; Windows then removes the file. Never delete it by hand.
rules.notes: hiberfil.sys holds memory contents for hibernate and Fast Startup; turning hibernation off also turns off Fast Startup.

rules.label: do_not_touch
rules.what: System Restore points and other volume data kept by Windows.
rules.reclaim: System Properties > System Protection > Configure: lower the space limit or delete restore points there.

rules.label: do_not_touch
rules.what: Data used by Windows components and Microsoft services (Defender, update, search and others).
rules.reclaim: Use Disk Cleanup or the owning feature's settings. Do not delete by hand.

rules.label: do_not_touch
rules.what: Installer package cache. Programs installed with these packages need them to repair or uninstall.
rules.reclaim: Uninstall programs you no longer use; their cached installers are removed with them.

rules.label: do_not_touch
rules.what: Installed programs.
rules.reclaim: Uninstall programs you no longer use: Settings > Apps > Installed apps. Deleting program folders by hand leaves broken entries behind.

rules.label: do_not_touch
rules.what: Programs installed for your user only (no admin install).
rules.reclaim: Uninstall programs you no longer use: Settings > Apps > Installed apps.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Microsoft Edge cache: copies of web pages and scripts, downloaded again when needed.
rules.reclaim: Edge: Settings > Privacy, search and services > Clear browsing data > Cached images and files. Or close Edge and delete the contents.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Google Chrome cache: copies of web pages and scripts, downloaded again when needed.
rules.reclaim: Chrome: Settings > Privacy and security > Delete browsing data > Cached images and files.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Brave cache: copies of web pages and scripts, downloaded again when needed.
rules.reclaim: Brave: Settings > Privacy and security > Delete browsing data > Cached images and files.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Firefox cache: copies of web pages and scripts, downloaded again when needed.
rules.reclaim: Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Cookies and Site Data > Clear Data > Cached Web Content.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Browser profile: history, saved passwords, cookies, extensions and settings.
rules.reclaim: Clear what you do not need from the browser's own settings. Deleting the folder signs you out everywhere and loses local data.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Cache of a desktop app built on Chromium (Electron): copies of web content, rebuilt when needed.
rules.reclaim: Close the app, then delete the contents.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Temporary Internet files used by Windows and older apps.
rules.reclaim: Disk Cleanup > Temporary Internet Files.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: File Explorer thumbnail and icon cache, rebuilt when needed.
rules.reclaim: Disk Cleanup > Thumbnails.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Graphics shader cache. Games and apps rebuild it; the first start after clearing can be slower.
rules.reclaim: Disk Cleanup > DirectX Shader Cache, or close games and delete the contents.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Downloaded NVIDIA driver installers.
rules.reclaim: Delete the contents once the driver is installed.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: VS Code caches, including data for old versions and downloaded extension packages.
rules.reclaim: Close VS Code, then delete the contents.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Installed VS Code extensions.
rules.reclaim: Uninstall extensions you do not use from the Extensions view in VS Code.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: JetBrains IDE caches and indexes, rebuilt when needed.
rules.reclaim: In the IDE: File > Invalidate Caches. Folders of IDE versions you no longer use can go entirely.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: npm download cache. Packages are downloaded again when needed.
rules.reclaim: npm cache clean --force

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Yarn download cache.
rules.reclaim: yarn cache clean

rules.label: safe
rules.what: pnpm content store shared by your projects.
rules.reclaim: pnpm store prune (removes only packages no project uses).

rules.label: safe
rules.what: pip download and wheel cache.
rules.reclaim: pip cache purge

rules.label: safe
rules.what: uv package cache.
rules.reclaim: uv cache clean (or uv cache prune to keep what is in use).

rules.label: safe
rules.what: NuGet package cache for .NET projects.
rules.reclaim: dotnet nuget locals all --clear

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Gradle dependency and build caches.
rules.reclaim: Stop Gradle daemons (gradle --stop), then delete. Files are downloaded again by the next build.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Maven local repository (downloaded dependencies).
rules.reclaim: Delete it; the next build downloads what it needs.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Cargo (Rust) download cache of crates.
rules.reclaim: Delete it; cargo downloads crates again when a build needs them.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Go build cache.
rules.reclaim: go clean -cache

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Conda package cache (downloaded packages and tarballs).
rules.reclaim: conda clean --all

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Installed JavaScript packages of a project. The project's package manager recreates them.
rules.reclaim: Delete it, then run npm install (or pnpm install / yarn) in the project when you work on it again.
rules.notes: Projects without a lock file may get newer package versions on reinstall.

rules.label: safe
rules.what: Compiled Python bytecode, recreated automatically.
rules.reclaim: Delete it.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Python virtual environment of a project.
rules.reclaim: Delete it and recreate it from the project's requirements or lock file (for example uv sync or pip install -r requirements.txt).
rules.notes: Packages installed by hand and not listed in a requirements file are lost.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Ollama model store (model weights in blobs, names in manifests).
rules.reclaim: List models with ollama list, remove one with ollama rm <name>. Do not delete files by hand: blobs are shared between models.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Ollama data: keys, history, logs and downloaded updates.
rules.reclaim: Models: ollama rm <name>. Logs and old update installers can be deleted with Ollama closed.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: LM Studio downloaded models.
rules.reclaim: Delete models you no longer use from LM Studio's My Models page.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Hugging Face download cache: models and datasets used by Python libraries.
rules.reclaim: huggingface-cli delete-cache (lets you pick which models to remove). Anything removed is downloaded again on next use.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: PyTorch hub cache: downloaded model weights.
rules.reclaim: Delete model folders you no longer use; they are downloaded again on next use.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Shared cache folder used by many developer tools. Most of it is rebuilt; some tools keep downloaded models here.
rules.reclaim: Look at the subfolders and clear each with its own tool.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Docker Desktop virtual disk: all images, containers, volumes and build cache.
rules.reclaim: docker system prune (add -a to also remove unused images; volumes are kept unless you add --volumes). The disk file may not shrink on its own afterwards. Never delete the file by hand.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Docker Desktop data: settings, logs and its virtual disk.
rules.reclaim: Clean up through Docker (docker system prune) or Docker Desktop's settings, not by deleting files.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Data of a Python packaging tool (uv or pip): its cache and, for uv, Python versions and tools it installed.
rules.reclaim: Clear the cache with the tool's own command (uv cache clean, pip cache purge); uninstall uv-managed Pythons with uv python uninstall.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: WSL Linux distribution disk (everything inside that Linux install).
rules.reclaim: Free space inside Linux first. To remove a distro you no longer need: wsl --list --verbose, then wsl --unregister <name> (deletes everything in it).

rules.label: do_not_touch
rules.what: Virtual machine disk used by the Claude desktop app.
rules.reclaim: Leave it to the app. If you no longer use the app, uninstall it first, then check whether this folder is still there.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Claude desktop app data: settings, logs, extensions and caches.
rules.reclaim: Caches inside can go with the app closed; settings and extensions are needed by the app.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Installed Steam games.
rules.reclaim: Uninstall games you do not play from the Steam library. Steam can download them again.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Your personal files.
rules.reclaim: Only you can decide. Move large files you want to keep to another drive, delete what you do not need.
rules.notes: DiskDelta never labels anything inside a personal folder as safe to remove.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Your downloads. Often holds old installers and archives you no longer need.
rules.reclaim: Sort by size or date and delete what you do not need. Installers can usually be downloaded again.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: User profile folder. Holds personal folders and app data.
rules.reclaim: Look at the folders inside.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: App data folder. Each app keeps its own folder inside.
rules.reclaim: Look at the folders inside; each belongs to an app.

rules.label: check_first
rules.what: Top of the drive.
rules.reclaim: Look at the folders inside.
